What is two-factor authentication (2FA)?

Two-factor authentication is a security method that requires two different forms of verification before allowing access to an account. This means that even if someone obtains your password, they would still need a second factor, such as a code generated in real time or a physical security key, to access your account.

Why is two-factor authentication important?

Two-factor authentication provides an additional layer of security by making it much more difficult for hackers or unauthorized people to access your accounts. Even if your password is compromised, the second factor of authentication acts as an additional barrier, protecting your sensitive data.

Activating dark mode in our software is easy. It is simply activated automatically with the configuration of the operating system you use.

We prefer to count what are we going to do, why we do it, and how it impacts those who use our systems every day.

Y 2026 empieza con two big decisions, designed for something very simple:that everything works better, with fewer errors, less stress and more predictability for everyone.

A new intermediate step:clients in staging

Until now, the path was quite direct:development → production

Y aunque siempre funcionó, la realidad es que los sistemas crecieron, los casos de uso se multiplicaron y el impacto de un cambio hoy es mucho mayor que hace algunos años.

For this reason, in 2026 we will formally incorporate a staging environment, with real clients who agree to participate in this intermediate step between testing and production.

What does this mean?

  • Real changes, with real data, but without affecting daily operation
  • Deeper validations before releasing something to everyone
  • Fewer hot fixes
  • More stable and predictable updates

Who will be staging?

Some specific clients, with prior consent, who:

  • Want to access new features sooner
  • Be willing to give real feedback
  • Get in return better quality, more stability and commercial benefits

This is not “trying unstable things”, it is exactly the opposite:it is protect production and improve everyone's experience.

The ticket module is no longer “just another module”

The second decision is something we have been thinking about for a long time.

The ticket system is no longer just “support.”

Today they live there:

  • Sales
  • Repairs
  • Call center
  • Remote support
  • Seguimientos internos
  • Completely different flows from each other

Forcing all that within the same logic no longer makes sense.

What are we going to do in 2026?

Let's go redefine, separate and specialize the ticket module:

  • Different flows depending on the type of care
  • Specific statuses and metrics for each area
  • Better operator experience
  • Better traceability for the client
  • Less friction, fewer unnecessary steps

The idea is not to “make it bigger”, but make it clearer, faster and more usable.

2026 is not about adding features for the sake of adding.

Se trata de order, try better, specialize and make systems more robust for real everyday use.

Thank you for being there, for using the system, for reporting errors, for suggesting improvements and for accompanying this growth.

See you in 2026.
